newsitem.title: UK: INDEPENDENT INS ON LOOK OUT FOR ACQUISITIONS.
newsitem.headline: INDEPENDENT INS ON LOOK OUT FOR ACQUISITIONS.

text.p: Britain's Independent Insurance Group Plc on Wednesday reported a 20 percent rise in first half profits but cautioned that it did not expect any significant upturn in the UK insurance market until late 1998.
However, the company expressed confidence about its own prospects despite the tough conditions and said it was on the look out for acquisitions.

In France and Spain, it was looking at commercial underwriters and in the UK was hoping that rationalisation of the european insurance scene would throw up opportunities to buy UK subsidiaries or accounts, Independent chief executive Michael Bright told Reuters.
"The company's market capitalisation is now over 400 million pounds, so our ambitions can be quite considerable," said Bright.
"We are prepared to issue paper for the right deal."
Echoing comments made by other insurers, Bright said that competition remained fierce, though the outlook was undoubtedly better than last year.
"There's perhaps a little less stupidity in the market than there was 12 months ago," said Bright.
"Commercial account business is slightly more protected than most and long term relationships with brokers and clients give us some stability but it's still difficult."
The liability account had hardened slightly against last year while commercial property was still competitive, he said.
The company expects long term policy arrangements, locking existing clients into five year deals based on the proven quality of their book, to help protect its book from competition.
Independent is also not as exposed to commodity type areas of insurance where price competition is at its worst.
"In the second half I expect underlying growth to go from neutral to positive and for that to continue into next year," said Bright.
A strong performance from the UK commercial account in the first six months of 1997 helped profits increase to 20 million pounds - ahead of market expectations.
The interim dividend was raised 18 percent to 6.25 pence per share.
Shares jumped on the results, adding 42-1/2 pence to 952-1/2 pence in early trading.
Bright described the performance as "encouraging" despite the tough competition and new participants continuing to enter every part of the company's business.
Reported gross written premiums rose 16 percent to 269.9 million pounds, due to the long-term policy arrangements now offered by the group.
However, the underlying position was flat, affected by a reduction in motor income as well as a fall in premium at its French subsidiary Independent SA.
Investment gains rose to 5.9 million pounds reflecting the decision late last year to limit exposure to equities to 30 percent of total investments.
